title: AppTest does not discover installed CCv2 components, so file-backed JS/CSS components fail under testing but work under `streamlit run`
body:
### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary A `st.components.v2` component that declares **file-backed** JS/CSS assets (e.g. `css="assets/style.css"` / `js="assets/script.js"`) works fine under `streamlit run`, but raises a `StreamlitAPIException` when the same app is invoked through `AppTest`: ``` StreamlitAPIException: Component 'mycomp.demo' must be declared in pyproject.toml with asset_dir to use file-backed css. ``` As an example, AppTest cannot import `streamlit-bokeh`. This seems to be a regression introduced in Streamlit 1.56.0. (works in 1.51.0–1.55.0; fails in 1.56.0–1.58.0) ### Reproducible Code Example Example using e.g. streamlit_bokeh: ```python from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest def app(): from streamlit_bokeh import streamlit_bokeh import streamlit as st st.success("Done") def test_app(): at = AppTest.from_function(app).run() assert at.success[0].value == "Done" ``` I also confirmed the issue appears with a custom component. For completeness, here's an example minimal component that also shows the same error when imported under AppTest:
`pyproject.toml`: ```toml [project] name = "mycomp" version = "0.0.1" dependencies = ["streamlit"] [[tool.streamlit.component.components]] name = "demo" asset_dir = "assets" [build-system] requires = ["setuptools"] build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta" [tool.setuptools] packages = ["mycomp"] ``` `mycomp/__init__.py`: ```python from streamlit.components.v2 import component mycomp = component( "mycomp.demo", html='
hi
', css="assets/style.css", js="assets/script.js", ) ``` `mycomp/assets/style.css`: ```css #mycomp { color: rebeccapurple; } ``` `mycomp/assets/script.js`: ```js console.log("mycomp loaded"); ```
### Steps To Reproduce `pytest test_demo_app.py`: fails ### Expected Behavior `AppTest` should resolve installed CCv2 components the same way `streamlit run` does, and the test should pass ### Current Behavior The test fails with: ``` demo_app.py:1 in from mycomp import mycomp mycomp/__init__.py:3 in mycomp = component("mycomp.demo", ... css="assets/style.css" ...) streamlit/components/v2/__init__.py:524 in component streamlit/components/v2/__init__.py:141 in _create_component_callable streamlit/components/v2/__init__.py:89 in _register_component streamlit/components/v2/component_definition_resolver.py:132 in build_definition_with_validation streamlit/components/v2/component_definition_resolver.py:107 in _resolve_entry StreamlitAPIException: Component 'mycomp.demo' must be declared in pyproject.toml with asset_dir to use file-backed css. ``` ### Is this a regression? - [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit: **1.58.0** (also fails on 1.56.0, 1.57.0; works on ≤1.55.0) - pytest: 9.0.3 - Python: 3.11 - OS: Linux ### Additional Information I think the issue relates to how the component manager discovers files: ```python from streamlit.components.v2.component_manager import BidiComponentManager m1 = BidiComponentManager() # what AppTest creates print(m1.get_component_asset_root("mycomp.demo")) # -> None m2 = BidiComponentManager() # what Runtime does m2.discover_and_register_components(start_file_watching=False) print(m2.get_component_asset_root("mycomp.demo")) # -> .../mycomp/assets ``` A fix could eb to have `AppTest._run()` call `discover_and_register_components(start_file_watching=False)` on the `BidiComponentManager` it assigns to the mock runtime, so installed v2 components resolve identically under test and under `streamlit run`.

## Triage Analysis

This is a confirmed regression in `AppTest` (introduced in 1.56.0): apps using `st.components.v2` components with **file-backed** `css=`/`js=` assets (e.g. `streamlit-bokeh`, or any package that declares `[[tool.streamlit.component.components]]` with an `asset_dir` in `pyproject.toml`) raise `StreamlitAPIException: Component '...' must be declared in pyproject.toml with asset_dir to use file-backed css.` under `pytest`/`AppTest`, even though the same app runs fine under `streamlit run`.

**Likely root cause** — confirmed by inspecting the code:

- In `lib/streamlit/testing/v1/app_test.py` (line 344), `AppTest._run()` assigns a fresh `BidiComponentManager()` to the mock runtime, but **never calls** `discover_and_register_components(...)` on it. So `manager.get_component_asset_root(component_key)` returns `None`.
- In `lib/streamlit/components/v2/component_definition_resolver.py` (around line 106–110), when `asset_root is None` and the user passes a path-like `css=`/`js=` value, the resolver raises the `StreamlitAPIException` reported above.
- `streamlit run` works because `Runtime` (in `lib/streamlit/runtime/runtime.py`) calls `discover_and_register_components(...)` during startup, which pre-populates the manager with all installed packaged components and their `asset_dir`s.

The fix proposed by the reporter — having `AppTest._run()` invoke `discover_and_register_components(start_file_watching=False)` on the mock runtime's `BidiComponentManager` — looks correct and consistent with how the real runtime initializes the registry.

### Related Issues

- [#14274 — `AppTest` crashes with `TypeError` when running apps that use `st.components.v2` custom components](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/14274) (closed): Same surface area (AppTest + CCv2 components). Different symptom (`TypeError: bad argument type for built-in operation` in `_bidi_component`) but stems from the same general gap in CCv2 support inside `AppTest`. Worth checking that the fix here doesn't reintroduce that crash and that both regressions are fully covered by tests.
- [#10574 — `streamlit-bokeh` missing Python 3.9 support due to bokeh3 version](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10574) (open): Tangentially related — `streamlit-bokeh` is the component called out in this report as a real-world reproducer. Not a duplicate, just useful context.
